      01
      About
    
    
      I am a Master of Computer Science student at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, working on robot learning, world-action models, and multimodal representation learning.
      I am currently conducting robot learning research with the MSC Lab at UC Berkeley.
      
        Prior to UIUC, I was admitted to the PhD program in Finance at the University of Rochester, where I later earned a master’s degree. Deciding to master out and restart on a new path was one of the most difficult but also one of the most important decisions in my academic journey. My training at Rochester provided me with a strong foundation in research, quantitative reasoning, and principled problem formulation. Over time, I realized that my core interests lie in AI and robotics, with the goal of building intelligent systems that can perceive, reason, and act in the real world. This experience not only shaped my research perspective, but also gave me the clarity and conviction to pursue the problems that matter most to me.
        I received my bachelor’s degree in Financial Technology, with a second major in Computer Science, from the University of Hong Kong, where I built a strong foundation in quantitative analysis and computing, and developed an early interest in machine learning through coursework.

      03
      Research
    
    
      My research focuses on learning representations and world-action models that connect visual perception to physically grounded robot behavior.
      
        
          A
          
            Learning action priors from video
            Addressing data scarcity in robot learning by extracting reusable motion and interaction priors from large-scale human videos for cross-embodiment transfer.
          
        
        
          B
          
            Geometry-aware multimodal alignment
            Developing representation spaces that capture heterogeneous semantics via mixed geometries, and enabling dynamic alignment across modalities at multiple levels.
          
        
        
          C
          
            World-action models for embodied intelligence
            Exploring models that jointly capture scene structure, physical dynamics, and action consequences to support generalizable planning and control.
          
        
      
    
  

  
    
      04
      Selected work
    
    
      
        
          Video foundation models · Pose estimation
          2026
        
        ChildPose: Foundation for Children Pose Modeling
        Manuscript under review
        ChildPose adapts pretrained pose backbones to child-centric video through memory-augmented temporal attention and age-aware co-training. The project also introduces a human-in-the-loop data construction pipeline that uses model failures to guide review and correction, producing consistent gains across multiple backbone families under subject-held-out evaluation.
        Manuscript under review
      
      
        
          Multimodal representation learning
          2026
        
        ProCLIP: Product Space Multimodal Contrastive Alignment
        Jiakai Chen and Hangke Sui · GRaM Workshop @ ICLR 2026
        This work introduces a mixed-curvature product space combining hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean manifolds to capture hierarchical and compositional multimodal structure. Its geometry-aware CLIP objective and lightweight manifold-specific projection heads improve Recall@1 by 2–7% over single-manifold baselines on Flickr30k and MSCOCO image–text retrieval.
